stem: Which of the following best describes a file, as defined in the chapter?
options: A temporary area in RAM that holds the variables while a program is running
A named location on secondary storage where data are kept permanently for later access
A named variable in a Python program that stores a sequence of characters
A part of the processor that keeps the output of the most recent program run
explanation: Correct option: (B). A file is a named location on secondary storage media where data are stored permanently, so they can be reused after the program ends. RAM and variables last only while a program executes, and a variable is not a file. The processor does not store files.

stem: A text file stores three lines of text. When the file is opened in a text editor, how does the editor know where each line ends?
options: The editor counts a fixed number of 80 characters and then begins a new line
Each line is saved in a separate block of the disk under its own file name
The editor begins a new line wherever it finds a comma (,) or a tab (\t)
Every line ends with a special End of Line character, by default the newline (\n)
explanation: Correct option: (D). Each line of a text file is terminated by a special character called End of Line (EOL); in Python the default EOL is the newline character \n. When the editor meets this character it shows the rest of the content from a new line. Lines are not fixed at 80 characters, are not stored as separate files, and commas or tabs only separate values within a line.

Reason (R): The bytes of a binary file represent actual content such as images, audio or executable code rather than ASCII values of characters.

Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

stem: Meera types only her name in Notepad and saves it as name.txt. She types the same name in a word processor and saves it as name.docx. The .txt file is a few bytes in size, but the .docx file is several kilobytes. What best explains the difference?

The .txt file squeezes each character into a single bit before it is saved
The .docx file uses a full kilobyte of storage for every character typed
Notepad keeps only the first few characters of the name and drops the rest
explanation: Correct option: (A). A text file stores only the ASCII equivalent of its characters (one byte per character here), so a short name takes only a few bytes. A .docx file additionally stores information such as the author's name, page settings, font type and size, and creation and modification dates, which adds kilobytes. Characters are not stored in one bit, a word processor does not use a kilobyte per character, and Notepad saves the whole name.
